# Atleato UI Audit — Why It Reads as AI-Generated

**Honest answer:** because most of it WAS generated by AI design tools earlier in this session. The visual language we landed on has 6 specific "AI tells" that experienced eyes pick up immediately.

This document names each one with the file:line evidence, then proposes 3 different human-designed directions to pick from.

---

## The 6 AI Tells Your Eye Is Catching

### 1. "Perfect" grid — every spacing is on the 4/8/12/16/24/32 ladder
- Every padding/margin in `constants/theme.ts` is `4 8 12 16 24 32 48`
- Every component obeys it religiously
- Humans deviate: a hand-designed UI has 13px somewhere because the eye said so

### 2. The Anton + JetBrains Mono + Inter triad
Used on EVERY screen, in the SAME hierarchical role:
- `Anton` for display headlines
- `JetBrains Mono` for "//-style" mono labels (`// YOUR LINEUP`, `// LIVE STATUS`)
- `Inter` for body
This three-font tech-magazine layout pattern is one of the strongest AI-design tells in 2025-26. It's the visual equivalent of "ChatGPT writes everything in bullet points."

Examples:
- `app/(tabs)/index.tsx` — `Fonts.display`, `Fonts.mono`, `Fonts.body`
- `app/(tabs)/coach.tsx` — same
- `app/squads.tsx` — same
- Every marketing page in `docs/` — same

### 3. Volt green `#dfff1f` everywhere
- Used as accent on every persona, every CTA, every chart, every active state
- Real human-designed apps use accent sparingly — Spotify green appears MAYBE 4 times per screen
- Atleato uses lime on ~12 elements per screen

### 4. Hexagons & polygons as identity primitives
- The polygon "A" in `assets/logo/logo-icon.svg`
- Hexagonal Vanguard badge on `docs/upsell.html`
- Hex-shaped stats cards on marketing pages
Polygons feel "generative-AI-aesthetic" in 2026 the way drop-shadows felt "Web 2.0" in 2008.

### 5. The "// uppercase mono kicker" pattern
Used on EVERY section:
- `// YOUR LINEUP` (welcome email)
- `// THIS IS HOW TRAINING STARTS` (showreel)
- `// LIVE FORM COACH` (showreel scene 4)
- `// REAL-WORLD MODE` (showreel scene 5)
This is the visual signature of "I was generated by an LLM in 2025." A single rare instance is OK. Eight of them in a row is the tell.

### 6. Generic emoji for icons
- `🔥` for streak
- `⚡` for legend
- `🏆` for champion
- `📞` for call
- `🎙️` for voice
- `🍽` for nutrition
Hand-designed apps invest in a custom icon set or use a single consistent library (Lucide, Heroicons, SF Symbols, Feather). Using OS emoji is the universal "MVP-was-AI-generated" signal.

---

## What "Human-Designed" Actually Means

It does NOT mean "make it ugly to look human." It means:

1. Pick ONE accent color and use it ≤ 5 times per screen
2. Pick TWO type families, not three
3. Let SOME alignment be deliberately off-grid (the "13px" rule)
4. Use a single coherent icon family (we recommend Lucide — free, consistent, looks intentional)
5. Drop the `//-mono-kicker` pattern entirely OR use it max once per screen
6. Choose ONE structural metaphor and apply it everywhere (cards? lists? timeline? — not all three on one screen)

---

## 3 Concrete Directions — Pick One

### 🟢 Direction A — "Apple Notes meets Strava"
- **Vibe:** clean, calm, premium-feeling
- **Type:** Inter only (one family, two weights — 400 + 700)
- **Color:** dark mode stays, lime accent reduced to JUST the active tab and primary CTA
- **Icons:** Lucide icon set, monochrome, all 1.5px stroke
- **Layout:** generous whitespace, no `//` mono kickers, no Anton display
- **Differentiation:** comes from copy voice, not visual complexity
- **Effort:** ~6 hrs to retheme all screens
- **Best for:** investor / press / Apple Watch crowd
- **Risk:** loses some of the current "aggressive" energy

### 🟠 Direction B — "Cron Calendar meets Notion"
- **Vibe:** sharp, dense, productivity-tool premium
- **Type:** Söhne or Inter (one family), display weight for headlines only
- **Color:** off-white surfaces (yes — light mode), single dark accent per persona
- **Icons:** Lucide, 2px stroke, with named labels under each
- **Layout:** information density, table-like rhythm
- **Effort:** ~10 hrs (also requires the light-theme work)
- **Best for:** quantitative users who care about data
- **Risk:** loses persona drama — every coach feels the same visually

### 🔴 Direction C — "Nike Training Club meets Telegram"
- **Vibe:** energetic, photo-forward, bold typography
- **Type:** Inter + ONE custom display font for personas (we'd license one — ~$200)
- **Color:** persona accent stays prominent but volt green moves to ONLY system actions (toggles, switches)
- **Icons:** custom 24x24 outlined set (we'd commission — ~$1500 OR I generate via prompts)
- **Layout:** edge-to-edge hero images, bottom CTA always anchored, full-bleed cards
- **Effort:** ~16 hrs + design budget
- **Best for:** mass-market fitness audience, app-store featuring
- **Risk:** highest cost, longest timeline

---

## My Honest Recommendation

**Direction A** for launch. Reasons:

1. Lowest effort, fastest to ship — you're at the corner of launch
2. Removes the strongest AI tells (volt-green overuse, three-font triad, mono kickers, emoji icons) with the smallest code surface
3. Doesn't require any design budget or external assets
4. Reversible — if it feels too tame post-launch, you can move toward B or C with new screens

Then post-launch, A/B test against either B or C with the live audience.

---

## What I CAN'T Do Inside Cursor/Claude Code

- Design a new icon family from scratch (or rather, I can attempt it but the result will read as AI-generated again — same loop)
- Pick a custom display font for you — that's a taste decision
- Tell you whether your audience would prefer A, B, or C — that's market research

What I CAN do once you pick a direction:
- Retheme the entire `constants/theme.ts`
- Update every screen with the new spacing/type/color rules
- Replace emoji with Lucide icons (free, programmatic install via `lucide-react-native`)
- Add a light-mode theme if Direction B is chosen
- Build a tiny `useTheme()` swap so we can A/B in the app itself

---

## Light Mode — What It Would Look Like

You asked specifically about white UI. Here's what would change vs. dark:

| Token | Dark (current) | Light variant |
|---|---|---|
| `bg` | `#0a0b0d` | `#fafaf7` (warm cream, not pure white) |
| `surface` | `#15171b` | `#ffffff` |
| `text` | `#f5f5f4` | `#0a0b0d` |
| `text-secondary` | `rgba(245,245,244,0.62)` | `rgba(10,11,13,0.62)` |
| `border` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.07)` | `rgba(0,0,0,0.07)` |
| `primary` (volt) | `#dfff1f` | `#0a0b0d` (text-on-light) OR `#b4d018` if we keep volt |

Things that DON'T translate well to light:
- The pulsing volt-green glows (rgba(212,255,61,.35)) — look weird on white
- The dark phone mockups in marketing — would need re-mocking
- The Anthropic-designed welcome email — needs separate light theme

Effort to add light mode properly: ~4 hours. Effort to mock ONE screen for you to evaluate: ~30 min.

**My recommendation:** if you pick Direction A, mocking the dashboard in light mode is a 30-min exercise so you can decide before I commit to a full rebuild. Tell me to go and I'll do it.
